Hence, by continuity of $^*$-homomorphisms, $$ \begin{aligned} \gamma_{R}(\psi(a))_{i}(x) &=\lim_{n\to\infty}\gamma_{R}(\psi(w_{n}))_{i}(x)\\ &=\lim_{n\to\infty}\operatorname{diag}\left(\gamma_{S}(w_{n})_{i_{1}}(x),\gamma_{S}(w_{n})_{i_{2}}(h^{\beta_{1}}(x)),\ldots,\gamma_{S}(w_{n})_{i_{q}}(h^{\beta_{q-1}}(x))\right)\\ &=\operatorname{diag}\left(\gamma_{S}(a)_{i_{1}}(x),\gamma_{S}(a)_{i_{2}}(h^{\beta_{1}}(x)),\ldots,\gamma_{S}(a)_{i_{q}}(h^{\beta_{q-1}}(x))\right), \end{aligned} $$ which yields the desired diagonal decomposition and completes the proof of \autoref{diagonal inclusion}.
nodes.statement_short: Check the diagonal decomposition on the generators f and ug using gamma_S, gamma_R and the return decomposition, then extend by continuity.

nodes.name: Return decomposition
nodes.statement: Fix $1\leq i\leq l (R)$ and $x\in X_{i}^{R}\setminus Y_{i}^{R}=\lambda_{R}^{-1}(n_{i}^{R})$. By \autoref{returning}, there are indices $1\leq i_{1},\ldots,i_{q}\leq l (S)$ such that: \begin{enumerate} \item $n_{i_{1}}^{S}+\cdots+n_{i_{q}}^{S}=n_{i}^{R}$; \item for all $1\leq k\leq n_{i}^{R}$, $h^{k}(x)\in S$ if and only if $k=\beta_{j}$ for some $1\leq j\leq q$, where $\beta_{j}:=n_{i_{1}}^{S}+\cdots+n_{i_{j}}^{S}$; \item for all $1\leq j\leq q$, $h^{\beta_{j-1}}(x)\in X_{i_{j}}^{S}\setminus Y_{i_{j}}^{S}$ (here $\beta_{0}:=0$, so that $x\in X_{i_{1}}^{S}\setminus Y_{i_{1}}^{S}$).
nodes.statement_short: Apply the return lemma to x

nodes.name: Apply the return lemma
nodes.statement: Fix $1\leq i\leq l (R)$ and $x\in X_{i}^{R}\setminus Y_{i}^{R}=\lambda_{R}^{-1}(n_{i}^{R})$. By \autoref{returning}, there are indices $1\leq i_{1},\ldots,i_{q}\leq l (S)$ such that:
nodes.statement_short: Get indices i_1..i_q with:

nodes.name: Property (1)
nodes.statement_short: Return times add up

nodes.name: Property (2)
nodes.statement: for all $1\leq k\leq n_{i}^{R}$, $h^{k}(x)\in S$ if and only if $k=\beta_{j}$ for some $1\leq j\leq q$, where $\beta_{j}:=n_{i_{1}}^{S}+\cdots+n_{i_{j}}^{S}$;
nodes.statement_short: Returns to S at the partial sums beta_j

nodes.name: Property (3)
nodes.statement: for all $1\leq j\leq q$, $h^{\beta_{j-1}}(x)\in X_{i_{j}}^{S}\setminus Y_{i_{j}}^{S}$ (here $\beta_{0}:=0$, so that $x\in X_{i_{1}}^{S}\setminus Y_{i_{1}}^{S}$).
nodes.statement_short: Intermediate points in X minus Y

nodes.name: Goal
nodes.statement: Let us show that $x$ decomposes into $h^{\beta_{0}}(x)=x,h^{\beta_{1}}(x),\ldots,h^{\beta_{q-1}}(x)$ under $\psi$.
nodes.statement_short: Show x decomposes into the return points under psi

nodes.name: Generators f
nodes.statement: Suppose that $f\in C(T)$. Let us begin by verifying that \begin{equation} \begin{aligned} \gamma_{R}(\psi(f))_{i}(x)=\operatorname{diag}\left(\gamma_{S}(f)_{i_{1}}(x),\gamma_{S}(f)_{i_{2}}(h^{\beta_{1}}(x)),\ldots,\gamma_{S}(f)_{i_{q}}(h^{\beta_{q-1}}(x))\right). \end{aligned} \end{equation} Fix $1\leq j\leq q$. By \autoref{function identification}, $$ \begin{aligned} \gamma_{S}(f)_{i_{j}}(h^{\beta_{j-1}}(x))&=\operatorname{diag}\left(f(h(h^{\beta_{j-1}}(x))),\ldots,f(h^{n_{i_{j}}^{S}}(h^{\beta_{j-1}}(x)))\right)\\ &=\operatorname{diag}\left(f(h^{\beta_{j-1}+1}(x)),\ldots,f(h^{\beta_{j}}(x))\right). \end{aligned} $$ Hence, $$ \begin{aligned} &\operatorname{diag}\left(\gamma_{S}(f)_{i_{1}}(x),\gamma_{S}(f)_{i_{2}}(h^{\beta_{1}}(x)),\ldots,\gamma_{S}(f)_{i_{q}}(h^{\beta_{q-1}}(x))\right)\\ =&\operatorname{diag}\left(f(h^{\beta_{0}+1}(x)),\ldots,f(h^{\beta_{1}}(x)),\ldots\ldots,f(h^{\beta_{q-1}+1}(x)),\ldots,f(h^{\beta_{q}}(x))\right)\\ =&\operatorname{diag}\left(f(h(x)),\ldots,f(h^{n_{i}^{R}}(x))\right)\\ =&\gamma_{R}(f)_{i}(x), \end{aligned} $$ which yields \autoref{diagonal f}.
nodes.statement_short: Check the diagonal form on f in C(T)

nodes.name: Target identity
nodes.statement: Suppose that $f\in C(T)$. Let us begin by verifying that \begin{equation} \begin{aligned} \gamma_{R}(\psi(f))_{i}(x)=\operatorname{diag}\left(\gamma_{S}(f)_{i_{1}}(x),\gamma_{S}(f)_{i_{2}}(h^{\beta_{1}}(x)),\ldots,\gamma_{S}(f)_{i_{q}}(h^{\beta_{q-1}}(x))\right). \end{aligned} \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: State the identity for f

nodes.name: Concatenate diagonals
nodes.statement: Fix $1\leq j\leq q$. By \autoref{function identification}, $$ \begin{aligned} \gamma_{S}(f)_{i_{j}}(h^{\beta_{j-1}}(x))&=\operatorname{diag}\left(f(h(h^{\beta_{j-1}}(x))),\ldots,f(h^{n_{i_{j}}^{S}}(h^{\beta_{j-1}}(x)))\right)\\ &=\operatorname{diag}\left(f(h^{\beta_{j-1}+1}(x)),\ldots,f(h^{\beta_{j}}(x))\right). \end{aligned} $$ Hence, $$ \begin{aligned} &\operatorname{diag}\left(\gamma_{S}(f)_{i_{1}}(x),\gamma_{S}(f)_{i_{2}}(h^{\beta_{1}}(x)),\ldots,\gamma_{S}(f)_{i_{q}}(h^{\beta_{q-1}}(x))\right)\\ =&\operatorname{diag}\left(f(h^{\beta_{0}+1}(x)),\ldots,f(h^{\beta_{1}}(x)),\ldots\ldots,f(h^{\beta_{q-1}+1}(x)),\ldots,f(h^{\beta_{q}}(x))\right)\\ =&\operatorname{diag}\left(f(h(x)),\ldots,f(h^{n_{i}^{R}}(x))\right)\\ =&\gamma_{R}(f)_{i}(x), \end{aligned} $$ which yields \autoref{diagonal f}.
nodes.statement_short: Diagonals along consecutive return segments concatenate to gamma_R(f)

nodes.name: Generators ug
nodes.statement: Next, suppose $g\in C_{0}(T\setminus S)$. Let us show that \begin{equation} \begin{aligned} \gamma_{R}(\psi(ug))_{i}(x)=\operatorname{diag}\left(\gamma_{S}(ug)_{i_{1}}(x),\gamma_{S}(ug)_{i_{2}}(h^{\beta_{1}}(x)),\ldots,\gamma_{S}(ug)_{i_{q}}(h^{\beta_{q-1}}(x))\right). \end{aligned} \end{equation} By \autoref{ufunction identification}, $$ \begin{aligned} \gamma_{R}(ug)_{i}(x)= \begin{pmatrix} 0 & & & & \\ g(h(x)) & 0 & & & \\ & g(h^{2}(x)) & \ddots & &\\ & & \ddots & 0 &\\ & & & g(h^{n_{i}^{R}-1}(x)) & 0 \end{pmatrix} \end{aligned}. $$ For $1\leq j\leq q$, we have $h^{\beta_{j}}(x)\in S$ by property (2) above, so that $g(h^{\beta_{j}}(x))=0$. Hence, partitioning $\{1,2,\ldots,n_{i}^{R}\}$ into the sets $\{\beta_{j-1}+1,\ldots,\beta_{j}\}$ for $1\leq j\leq q$, we may view $\gamma_{R}(ug)_{i}(x)$ as a block-diagonal matrix $\operatorname{diag}(B_{1},\ldots,B_{q})$, where $$ \begin{aligned} B_{j}&:=\begin{pmatrix} 0 & & & & \\ g(h^{\beta_{j-1}+1}(x)) & 0 & & & \\ & g(h^{\beta_{j-1}+2}(x)) & \ddots & &\\ & & \ddots & 0 &\\ & & & g(h^{\beta_{j}-1}(x)) & 0 \end{pmatrix} =\gamma_{S}(ug)_{i_{j}}(h^{\beta_{j-1}}(x)), \end{aligned} $$ which yields \autoref{diagonal ug}.
nodes.statement_short: Check the diagonal form on ug

nodes.name: Subdiagonal form
nodes.statement: By \autoref{ufunction identification}, $$ \begin{aligned} \gamma_{R}(ug)_{i}(x)= \begin{pmatrix} 0 & & & & \\ g(h(x)) & 0 & & & \\ & g(h^{2}(x)) & \ddots & &\\ & & \ddots & 0 &\\ & & & g(h^{n_{i}^{R}-1}(x)) & 0 \end{pmatrix} \end{aligned}. $$
nodes.statement_short: Write gamma_R(ug) as a subdiagonal matrix

nodes.name: Vanishing at returns
nodes.statement: For $1\leq j\leq q$, we have $h^{\beta_{j}}(x)\in S$ by property (2) above, so that $g(h^{\beta_{j}}(x))=0$.
nodes.statement_short: g vanishes at return points to S

nodes.name: Blocks
nodes.statement: Hence, partitioning $\{1,2,\ldots,n_{i}^{R}\}$ into the sets $\{\beta_{j-1}+1,\ldots,\beta_{j}\}$ for $1\leq j\leq q$, we may view $\gamma_{R}(ug)_{i}(x)$ as a block-diagonal matrix $\operatorname{diag}(B_{1},\ldots,B_{q})$, where $$ \begin{aligned} B_{j}&:=\begin{pmatrix} 0 & & & & \\ g(h^{\beta_{j-1}+1}(x)) & 0 & & & \\ & g(h^{\beta_{j-1}+2}(x)) & \ddots & &\\ & & \ddots & 0 &\\ & & & g(h^{\beta_{j}-1}(x)) & 0 \end{pmatrix} =\gamma_{S}(ug)_{i_{j}}(h^{\beta_{j-1}}(x)), \end{aligned} $$ which yields \autoref{diagonal ug}.
nodes.statement_short: The subdiagonal splits into the gamma_S(ug) blocks

nodes.name: Continuity
nodes.statement: We have shown that $x$ decomposes into $h^{\beta_{0}}(x)=x,h^{\beta_{1}}(x),\ldots,h^{\beta_{q-1}}(x)$ under $\psi$ on the generators of $A_{S}$. Let us now use continuity to prove that this decomposition is maintained for all elements of $A_{S}$. Let $a\in A_{S}$ be arbitrary. By definition, we may write $a=\lim_{n\to\infty}w_{n}$, where for each $n\in\mathbb{N}$, $w_{n}$ is a word in $C(T)\cup uC_{0}(T\setminus S)\cup C_{0}(T\setminus S)u^{*}$. By \autoref{diagonal f} and \autoref{diagonal ug}, $$ \begin{aligned} \gamma_{R}(\psi(w_{n}))_{i}(x) =\operatorname{diag}\left(\gamma_{S}(w_{n})_{i_{1}}(x),\gamma_{S}(w_{n})_{i_{2}}(h^{\beta_{1}}(x)),\ldots,\gamma_{S}(w_{n})_{i_{q}}(h^{\beta_{q-1}}(x))\right) \end{aligned} $$ for all $n\in\mathbb{N}$. Hence, by continuity of $^*$-homomorphisms, $$ \begin{aligned} \gamma_{R}(\psi(a))_{i}(x) &=\lim_{n\to\infty}\gamma_{R}(\psi(w_{n}))_{i}(x)\\ &=\lim_{n\to\infty}\operatorname{diag}\left(\gamma_{S}(w_{n})_{i_{1}}(x),\gamma_{S}(w_{n})_{i_{2}}(h^{\beta_{1}}(x)),\ldots,\gamma_{S}(w_{n})_{i_{q}}(h^{\beta_{q-1}}(x))\right)\\ &=\operatorname{diag}\left(\gamma_{S}(a)_{i_{1}}(x),\gamma_{S}(a)_{i_{2}}(h^{\beta_{1}}(x)),\ldots,\gamma_{S}(a)_{i_{q}}(h^{\beta_{q-1}}(x))\right), \end{aligned} $$ which yields the desired diagonal decomposition and completes the proof of \autoref{diagonal inclusion}.
nodes.statement_short: Extend from words in the generators to all of A_S by continuity

nodes.name: Diagonal decomposition on f

nodes.name: Orbit-breaking subalgebras at a point have stable rank one
nodes.statement: Let $T$ be an infinite compact metric space and let $h\colon T\to T$ be a minimal homeomorphism. Given a non-isolated point $x\in T$, the orbit-breaking subalgebra $A_{\{x\}}$ of $A:=\mathrm{C^*}(\mathbb{Z},T,h)$ is a simple inductive limit of DSH algebras with diagonal maps. In particular, $A_{\{x\}}$ has stable rank one.
assumptions: Let $T$ be an infinite compact metric space and let $h\colon T\to T$ be a minimal homeomorphism
Given a non-isolated point $x\in T$
conclusions: the orbit-breaking subalgebra $A_{\{x\}}$ of $A:=\mathrm{C^*}(\mathbb{Z},T,h)$ is a simple inductive limit of DSH algebras with diagonal maps
$A_{\{x\}}$ has stable rank one
also_stated_at: every orbit-breaking subalgebra of the induced dynamical crossed product $\mathrm{C}^{*}(\mathbb{Z},T,h)$ associated to any non-isolated point is a simple inductive limit of DSH algebras with diagonal maps
nodes.label: Ax

nodes.name: Proof for orbit-breaking subalgebras
nodes.statement: Choose a sequence $S_{1}\supset S_{2}\supset\cdots$ of closed sets with non-empty interior such that $\bigcap_{n=1}^{\infty}S_{n}=\{x\}$. For each $n\in\mathbb{N}$, let $A_{S_{n}}\subset A$ denote the subalgebra as described above and let $\psi_{n}\colon A_{S_{n}}\to A_{S_{n+1}}$ denote the canonical inclusion. Since $\overline{\bigcup_{n=1}^{\infty}A_{S_{n}}}=A_{\{x\}}$, it follows by \autoref{putnam diagonal} that $A_{\{x\}}$ is an inductive limit of DSH algebras with diagonal maps. Moreover, by Theorem 1.2 of \cite{LP}, $A_{\{x\}}$ is simple (see Proposition 2.5 of \cite{xinP} for a proof). Therefore, by \autoref{main}, $A_{\{x\}}$ has stable rank one.
nodes.statement_short: Write A_{x} as the limit of A_{S_n} for shrinking S_n; inclusions are diagonal, the limit is simple (Lin-Phillips), so the main theorem applies.

nodes.name: Shrinking sets

For each $n\in\mathbb{N}$, let $A_{S_{n}}\subset A$ denote the subalgebra as described above and let $\psi_{n}\colon A_{S_{n}}\to A_{S_{n+1}}$ denote the canonical inclusion.
nodes.statement_short: Choose closed S_n shrinking to {x}; inclusions psi_n

nodes.name: Limit with diagonal maps
nodes.statement: Since $\overline{\bigcup_{n=1}^{\infty}A_{S_{n}}}=A_{\{x\}}$, it follows by \autoref{putnam diagonal} that $A_{\{x\}}$ is an inductive limit of DSH algebras with diagonal maps.
nodes.statement_short: A_{x} is the limit of the A_{S_n} with diagonal inclusions

nodes.name: Simplicity and main theorem
nodes.statement: Moreover, by Theorem 1.2 of \cite{LP}, $A_{\{x\}}$ is simple (see Proposition 2.5 of \cite{xinP} for a proof). Therefore, by \autoref{main}, $A_{\{x\}}$ has stable rank one.
nodes.statement_short: A_{x} is simple, so the main theorem gives stable rank one

nodes.name: Stable rank one for minimal dynamical crossed products
nodes.statement: Let $T$ be an infinite compact metric space and let $h\colon T\to T$ be a minimal homeomorphism. The dynamical crossed product $A:=\mathrm{C^*}(\mathbb{Z},T,h)$ has stable rank one.
assumptions: Let $T$ be an infinite compact metric space and let $h\colon T\to T$ be a minimal homeomorphism
conclusions: The dynamical crossed product $A:=\mathrm{C^*}(\mathbb{Z},T,h)$ has stable rank one
also_stated_at: for any infinite compact metric space $T$ and minimal homeomorphism $h\colon T\to T$, the associated dynamical crossed product $\mathrm{C^*}(\mathbb{Z},T,h)$ has stable rank one
nodes.label: main2

nodes.name: Proof of stable rank one for crossed products
nodes.statement: Let $x$ be any non-isolated point in $T$. By \autoref{Ax}, $A_{\{x\}}$ has stable rank one. Since $h$ is minimal and $T$ is infinite, $h^{n}(x)\not=x$ for all $n\in\mathbb{N}$. Thus, on combining Theorem 7.10 of \cite{phil2} with Theorem 4.6 of \cite{arcphil}, it follows that $A_{\{x\}}$ is a centrally large subalgebra of $A$. But by Theorem 6.3 of \cite{arcphil}, any infinite-dimensional unital simple separable $\mathrm{C}^*$-algebra containing a centrally large subalgebra with stable rank one must itself have stable rank one.
nodes.statement_short: A_{x} has stable rank one and is centrally large in A (Phillips; Archey-Phillips), and centrally large subalgebras transfer stable rank one.

nodes.name: Orbit-breaking subalgebra
nodes.statement: Let $x$ be any non-isolated point in $T$. By \autoref{Ax}, $A_{\{x\}}$ has stable rank one.
nodes.statement_short: A_{x} has stable rank one

nodes.name: Centrally large
nodes.statement: Since $h$ is minimal and $T$ is infinite, $h^{n}(x)\not=x$ for all $n\in\mathbb{N}$. Thus, on combining Theorem 7.10 of \cite{phil2} with Theorem 4.6 of \cite{arcphil}, it follows that $A_{\{x\}}$ is a centrally large subalgebra of $A$.
nodes.statement_short: A_{x} is centrally large in A (Phillips; Archey-Phillips)

nodes.name: Transfer
nodes.statement: But by Theorem 6.3 of \cite{arcphil}, any infinite-dimensional unital simple separable $\mathrm{C}^*$-algebra containing a centrally large subalgebra with stable rank one must itself have stable rank one.
nodes.statement_short: Stable rank one passes from a centrally large subalgebra to A

nodes.name: Toms–Winter conjecture for minimal dynamical crossed products
nodes.statement: Let $T$ be an infinite compact metric space and let $h\colon T\to T$ be a minimal homeomorphism. The dynamical crossed product $A:=\mathrm{C^*}(\mathbb{Z},T,h)$ is $\mathcal{Z}$-stable if and only if it has strict comparison of positive elements.
assumptions: Let $T$ be an infinite compact metric space and let $h\colon T\to T$ be a minimal homeomorphism
conclusions: The dynamical crossed product $A:=\mathrm{C^*}(\mathbb{Z},T,h)$ is $\mathcal{Z}$-stable if and only if it has strict comparison of positive elements
equivalent_conditions: it has strict comparison of positive elements
also_stated_at: for such crossed products, classifiability is determined solely by strict comparison
nodes.label: main3

nodes.name: Proof of the Toms–Winter corollary
nodes.statement: Let $x$ be any non-isolated point in $T$. By \autoref{Ax}, $A_{\{x\}}$ has stable rank one. Thus, by Theorem 9.6 of \cite{thi}, the Toms--Winter Conjecture (\autoref{Toms-Winter}) holds for $A_{\{x\}}$. In particular, $A_{\{x\}}$ is $\mathcal{Z}$-stable if and only if it has strict comparison of positive elements. But by Theorem 3.3 and Corollary 3.5 of \cite{ABP}, $A$ is $\mathcal{Z}$-stable if and only if $A_{\{x\}}$ is. Furthermore, by Theorem 6.14 of \cite{phil2}, $A$ has strict comparison if and only if $A_{\{x\}}$ does. Therefore, \autoref{main3} follows.
nodes.statement_short: Thiel's theorem gives Toms-Winter for A_{x} (stable rank one); Z-stability and strict comparison pass between A and A_{x} (Archey-Buck-Phillips; Phillips).

nodes.name: Toms-Winter for A_{x}
nodes.statement: Let $x$ be any non-isolated point in $T$. By \autoref{Ax}, $A_{\{x\}}$ has stable rank one. Thus, by Theorem 9.6 of \cite{thi}, the Toms--Winter Conjecture (\autoref{Toms-Winter}) holds for $A_{\{x\}}$. In particular, $A_{\{x\}}$ is $\mathcal{Z}$-stable if and only if it has strict comparison of positive elements.
nodes.statement_short: Thiel's theorem gives Toms-Winter for A_{x}

nodes.name: Transfer to A
nodes.statement: But by Theorem 3.3 and Corollary 3.5 of \cite{ABP}, $A$ is $\mathcal{Z}$-stable if and only if $A_{\{x\}}$ is. Furthermore, by Theorem 6.14 of \cite{phil2}, $A$ has strict comparison if and only if $A_{\{x\}}$ does. Therefore, \autoref{main3} follows.
nodes.statement_short: Z-stability and strict comparison pass between A and A_{x}

nodes.name: Deeley–Putnam–Strung orbit-breaking subalgebras have stable rank one
nodes.statement: Using the same ideas as those in the proof of \autoref{Ax}, one can show that the orbit-breaking simple subalgebras constructed by Deeley, Putnam, and Strung in \cite{DPS} also have stable rank one, despite possibly not being $\mathcal{Z}$-stable. Although, the closed subset of the underlying infinite compact metric space used in their construction need not be a singleton set, it still has the property that it meets every orbit exactly once, and thus, is a simple inductive limit of DSH algebras with diagonal maps.
nodes.statement_short: The same argument gives stable rank one for the Deeley-Putnam-Strung orbit-breaking subalgebras, which need not be Z-stable.
